# Thermo

Values strictly increase from the bulb to the tip of the thermometer.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

D(c) is the digit in cell c; V(c) is its value after any declared modifier, otherwise D(c). The line is the supplied cell sequence; |line| is its length. The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∀i ∈ [0,|line|−1): V(line[i]) < V(line[i+1])
```

Values strictly increase along the path from its bulb.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Thermo example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
thermo r1c1-r1c2
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2. 1 then 2 increases from the bulb.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=1. 2 then 1 decreases from the bulb.

# Modular

Every three consecutive digits have different remainders when divided by the stated modulus. On a two-cell line, the remainders differ.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |
| loop | Whether the line closes, joining its last cell back to its first. | false (open path). |
| modulus | The divisor used to take remainders. | 3; modulus ≥ 1. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

D(c) is the digit in cell c; V(c) is its value after any declared modifier, otherwise D(c). The line is the supplied cell sequence; |line| is its length. The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
m = modulus if present(modulus), else 3
∀s: start(line,3,s) → distinct_{rem(D(·),m)}(window(line,3,s))
∧ (¬loop ∧ |line|=2 → rem(D(line[0]),m) ≠ rem(D(line[1]),m))
```

Every window of three path positions has three distinct normalised remainders modulo modulus. An open two-cell line has different remainders. Loop windows wrap; modulus defaults to 3.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Modular example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
modular r1c1-r1c2-r1c3
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=3. 1, 2, 3 have remainders 1, 2, 0 modulo 3.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=4. 1, 2, 4 repeats remainder 1.

# Renban

The line contains different values that form a consecutive run, in any order.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. L has no repeated cell. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

D(c) is the digit in cell c; V(c) is its value after any declared modifier, otherwise D(c). The line is the supplied cell sequence; |line| is its length. The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
distinct_V(line) ∧ max_V(line)−min_V(line) = |line|−1
∧ ∀k ∈ [0,|line|): ∃c ∈ line: V(c)=min_V(line)+k
```

The V values are distinct and max(V)−min(V)=length−1. On integer values, every integer in that interval appears.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Renban example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
renban r1c1-r1c2-r1c3
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=1, r1c3=3. 2, 1, 3 contains the consecutive digits 1–3.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=1, r1c3=4. 2, 1, 4 misses 3 and has a gap in its run.

# Pair

The two values obey the stated relationship: a difference, ratio, total, multiple, inequality or shift.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| relation | The relationship keyword and any required whole-number value, for example difference 1. | Required. |
| cells | The two marked cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2. | Required. |

## Rule lines

Write the two cells in order, then a relationship keyword. Values in rule lines are whole numbers. The `relation` parameter declares these keyword forms; tools derive the grammar from that declaration.

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 difference 2` | The values differ by exactly 2. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 at-least 3` | The values differ by at least 3. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 ratio 3` | One value is three times the other. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 sum 10` | The values total 10. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 less` | The first value is less than the second. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 multiple` | The larger is an integer multiple of the smaller; two zeros also satisfy it. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 shift` | Both values are integers other than 5; they share exactly one of parity and being greater than 5. |

A dot's colour is drawing metadata. State its relationship with `pair`, whether the dot is grey, brown or another colour. [Kropki](kropki.md) names the two usual relationships: white is `difference 1`, black is `ratio 2`. The former `relation {"op":...}` form is replaced by these keywords.

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|cells|=2 ∧ pairRelation(relation,V(cells[0]),V(cells[1]))
```

The two cell values obey the supplied relation. The shared predicates define each relation: difference, ratio, sum, inequality, multiple or shift.

The shift relation is defined for integer values.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Pair example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
pair r1c1-r1c2 sum 10
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=3, r1c2=7. 3 and 7 add up to the stated total 10.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=3, r1c2=8. 3 and 8 add up to 11 instead of 10.

# Pair

The two values obey the stated relationship: a difference, ratio, total, multiple, inequality or shift.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| relation | The relationship keyword and any required whole-number value, for example difference 1. | Required. |
| cells | The two marked cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2. | Required. |

## Rule lines

Write the two cells in order, then a relationship keyword. Values in rule lines are whole numbers. The `relation` parameter declares these keyword forms; tools derive the grammar from that declaration.

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 difference 2` | The values differ by exactly 2. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 at-least 3` | The values differ by at least 3. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 ratio 3` | One value is three times the other. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 sum 10` | The values total 10. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 less` | The first value is less than the second. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 multiple` | The larger is an integer multiple of the smaller; two zeros also satisfy it. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 shift` | Both values are integers other than 5; they share exactly one of parity and being greater than 5. |

A dot's colour is drawing metadata. State its relationship with `pair`, whether the dot is grey, brown or another colour. [Kropki](kropki.md) names the two usual relationships: white is `difference 1`, black is `ratio 2`. The former `relation {"op":...}` form is replaced by these keywords.

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|cells|=2 ∧ pairRelation(relation,V(cells[0]),V(cells[1]))
```

The two cell values obey the supplied relation. The shared predicates define each relation: difference, ratio, sum, inequality, multiple or shift.

The shift relation is defined for integer values.

# N Mate

Count along the ray by the clue digit. That target digit plus the clue equals the cage total. Cage digits are different.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cell | The clue cell. | Required. |
| ray | The cells along the ray, nearest first. | Required. |
| cage | The cells in the cage. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
let n=D(cell); 1<=n<=|ray| ∧ n+D(ray[n-1])=sum_D(cage) ∧ distinct_D(cage)
```

The marked digit names a one-based position within ray. The marked and target digits sum to the cage total. Cage digits are distinct.

## Example

````markdown
title: N Mate example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules

n-mate cell "r1c1" ray ["r1c2","r1c3"] cage ["r1c4"]
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c4=3, r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=4. The clue and its selected ray digit add up to the cage total.

Breaks the rule: r1c4=4, r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=4. The selected ray digit gives the wrong total.

## Parameters


Every V value has parity named by parity: odd has absolute remainder 1, even remainder 0 modulo 2.

Electron digits around each atom add up to its stated total. All cells at or below the electron threshold are electrons; higher digits may also be chosen. Touching atoms share the same electron choices.

# Cage Expressions

Each cage total equals its expression. Letters stand for whole numbers and keep the same value throughout the rule. The distinct parameter gives different letters different values.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cages | The cells in each cage and its expression or relation, as stated in the definition. | Required. |
| distinct | Whether different letters must have different values. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∃letterValues:list<position>:
  |letterValues|=letterCount({g.expression:g∈cages}) ∧
  (∀g∈cages: defined(g.expression,letterValues) ∧ eval(g.expression,letterValues)=sum_D(g.cells))
  ∧ (distinct → ∀i,j∈[0,|letterValues|): i!=j → letterValues[i]!=letterValues[j])
```

There is a shared assignment of integers to letters such that each evaluated expression equals its cage total. distinct requires different letters to have different values. Division is exact with nonzero divisor; powers require a nonnegative integer exponent.

# Line Choice

The line satisfies between the stated minimum and maximum number of the listed line rules.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |
| kinds | The line rules available to choose from. | Required. |

| max | The greatest number of listed rules or different digits allowed. | Required. |
| loop | Whether the line closes, joining its last cell back to its first. | false (open path). |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
let selected=λoption:enum{renban,nabner,modular,entropic,parity}:
  (option="renban" ∧ |line|>0 ∧ distinctAt(line,λoccurrence:cell: D(occurrence)) ∧ max_D(line)-min_D(line)=|line|-1)
  ∨ (option="nabner" ∧ ∀i,j∈[0,|line|): i!=j → |D(line[i])-D(line[j])|!=1)
  ∨ (option="modular" ∧ ∀s∈[0,|line|): start(line,3,s,loop) → distinctAt(window(line,3,s,loop),λc:cell: classMod3(D(c))))
  ∨ (option="entropic" ∧ |𝔄|>0 ∧ |𝔄| mod 3=0 ∧ ∀s∈[0,|line|): start(line,3,s,loop) → distinctAt(window(line,3,s,loop),λc:cell: classEntropy(D(c))))
  ∨ (option="parity" ∧ ∀s∈[0,|line|): start(line,2,s,loop) → distinctAt(window(line,2,s,loop),λc:cell: classParity(D(c))));
min<=countWhere(kinds,selected)<=max
```

Count the entries of kinds whose defining checks accept this path; min ≤ count ≤ max. nabner permits repeats here. Class windows use three-position choice windows; parity uses two-position windows. An open two-cell modular or entropic choice is therefore vacuous, unlike its standalone kind.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=5. Neither renban nor nabner holds.

# Equality Cage

Cage digits are different. The number of low odd digits equals the number of high even digits; low even and high odd counts also match.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
distinct_D(cells) ∧ (∀c∈cells: D(c)!=(|𝔄|+1)/2)
∧ countWhere(cells,λc:cell: D(c)<(|𝔄|+1)/2 ∧ odd(D(c)))=countWhere(cells,λc:cell: D(c)>(|𝔄|+1)/2 ∧ ¬odd(D(c)))
∧ countWhere(cells,λc:cell: D(c)<(|𝔄|+1)/2 ∧ ¬odd(D(c)))=countWhere(cells,λc:cell: D(c)>(|𝔄|+1)/2 ∧ odd(D(c)))
```

Digits are distinct. Low-odd count equals high-even count and low-even count equals high-odd count. Low/high use the lower/upper halves of 1..n; an odd alphabet’s middle digit is forbidden.

# Hidden Modular

Choose the span by its stated extent. Every three consecutive digits in that span have different remainders when divided by 3.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |
| extent | How to choose the span: to-max, between-ends or first-x. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|𝔄|>0 ∧ ∃a,b∈[0,|cells|):
  a<=b ∧ ((extent="to-max" ∧ a=0 ∧ firstOccurrence(cells,𝔄[|𝔄|-1],b))
    ∨ (extent="between-ends" ∧ ∃i,j∈[0,|cells|): firstOccurrence(cells,𝔄[0],i)
       ∧ firstOccurrence(cells,𝔄[|𝔄|-1],j) ∧ a=minimumPosition(i,j) ∧ b=maximumPosition(i,j))
    ∨ (extent="first-x" ∧ a=0 ∧ |cells|>0 ∧ 1<=D(cells[0])<=|cells| ∧ b=D(cells[0])-1))
  ∧ ∀s∈[a,b-1): distinctAt(window(cells,3,s,false),λc:cell: classMod3(D(c)))
```

Choose the span from the clue through the maximum (to-max), between minimum and maximum inclusive (between-ends), or the first D(cells[0]) positions (first-x). Every triple in that span has three distinct remainders modulo 3.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Hidden Modular example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
hidden-modular r1c1-r1c2-r1c3 extent "first-x"
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=3, r1c2=1, r1c3=2. The first digit selects a three-cell span with all three remainders.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=3, r1c2=1, r1c3=4. The selected span repeats a remainder.

A missing endpoint or an invalid first-x extent cannot select a span, so the rule is false.

# Pair

The two values obey the stated relationship: a difference, ratio, total, multiple, inequality or shift.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| relation | The relationship keyword and any required whole-number value, for example difference 1. | Required. |
| cells | The two marked cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2. | Required. |

## Rule lines

Write the two cells in order, then a relationship keyword. Values in rule lines are whole numbers. The `relation` parameter declares these keyword forms; tools derive the grammar from that declaration.

| Form | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 difference 2` | The values differ by exactly 2. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 at-least 3` | The values differ by at least 3. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 ratio 3` | One value is three times the other. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 sum 10` | The values total 10. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 less` | The first value is less than the second. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 multiple` | The larger is an integer multiple of the smaller; two zeros also satisfy it. |
| `pair r1c1-r1c2 shift` | Both values are integers other than 5; they share exactly one of parity and being greater than 5. |

A dot's colour is drawing metadata. State its relationship with `pair`, whether the dot is grey, brown or another colour. [Kropki](kropki.md) names the two usual relationships: white is `difference 1`, black is `ratio 2`. The former `relation {"op":...}` form is replaced by these keywords.

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|cells|=2 ∧ pairRelation(relation,V(cells[0]),V(cells[1]))
```

The two cell values obey the supplied relation. The shared predicates define each relation: difference, ratio, sum, inequality, multiple or shift.

The shift relation is defined for integer values.

````markdown
```
````

Breaks the rule: r1c1=3, r1c2=8. 3 and 8 add up to 11 instead of 10.

# Pointing Thermo

Digits strictly increase from bulb to tip. Count outward along the ray by the tip digit: that cell contains the bulb digit.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |

| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|line|>0 ∧ (∀i∈[0,|line|-1): D(line[i])<D(line[i+1]))
∧ let x=D(line[|line|-1]); 1<=x<=|ray| ∧ D(ray[x-1])=D(line[0])
```

Digits strictly increase along cells. The tip digit names a one-based position on ray whose digit equals the bulb digit. The named position must be within the ray.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c4=4, r1c3=3. The selected ray cell contains 4 instead of the bulb 1.

# Yin Yang

Shade the board so each colour forms one connected group and every 2×2 contains both colours.

## Parameters

No parameters. It applies to the whole declared board and uses the shared shading answer.

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
connected({c ∈ C: shaded(c)}) ∧ connected({c ∈ C: ¬shaded(c)})
∧ ∀r ∈ [0,rows−1): ∀k ∈ [0,cols−1):
  (∃a ∈ window2(r,k): shaded(a)) ∧ (∃b ∈ window2(r,k): ¬shaded(b))
```

Both colours are nonempty and orthogonally connected; every 2×2 contains both colours.
This is a general authoring-library rule over the one typed shading answer, rather than a newly recognised decoded constraint.

# Modular

Every three consecutive digits have different remainders when divided by the stated modulus. On a two-cell line, the remainders differ.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |
| loop | Whether the line closes, joining its last cell back to its first. | false (open path). |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
modulus>=1 ∧ (∀s∈[0,|line|): start(line,3,s,loop) → distinctAt(window(line,3,s,loop),λc:cell: rem(D(c),modulus)))
∧ (¬loop ∧ |line|=2 → rem(D(line[0]),modulus)!=rem(D(line[1]),modulus))
```

Every window of three path positions has three distinct normalised remainders modulo modulus. An open two-cell line has different remainders. Loop windows wrap; modulus defaults to 3.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=4. 1, 2, 4 repeats remainder 1.

# Diagonal Lines

Each sufficiently long diagonal either stays in one digit class or repeats complete windows of all classes.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| classes | The digit classes to use: parity, remainder or alphabet thirds. | Required. |
| minLength | The shortest diagonal covered by the rule. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
(classes!="entropy" ∨ (|𝔄|>0 ∧ |𝔄| mod 3=0))
∧ ∀L∈boardDiagonals(): |L|>=maximumPair(3,minLength) →
  ((∃k∈classIds(classes): ∀c∈L: digitClass(classes,D(c))=k)
   ∨ (∀s∈[0,|L|-|classIds(classes)|+1):
     distinctAt(window(L,|classIds(classes)|,s,false),λc:cell: digitClass(classes,D(c)))))
```

Every board diagonal of length at least max(3,minLength) is constant in class or has every class once in each window of class-count positions.

## Example

````markdown
format: open-rules
title: Diagonal Lines example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read

  cols: 3
  symbols:
    - 1
    - 2
    - 3
    - 4
    - 5
    - 6
    - 7
    - 8
    - 9
---

```rules
diagonal-lines classes "parity" minLength 3
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r2c2=3, r3c3=5. This three-cell diagonal stays in one parity class.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=2, r2c2=3, r3c3=5. A diagonal changes class without the required repeating class windows.

# Shifter Line

Digits on the line cannot be 5. Within a region, neighbours are both odd or both even and both below or both above 5. At each region crossing, exactly one of those relationships changes.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
(∀c∈line:D(c)!=5)
∧ ∀i,j∈[0,|line|): consecutive(line,i,j,false) →
  let P=(odd(D(line[i]))↔odd(D(line[j]))); let Q=(high(D(line[i]))↔high(D(line[j])));
  (sameRegion(line[i],line[j]) → P ∧ Q) ∧ (¬sameRegion(line[i],line[j]) → ¬(P↔Q))
```

No digit is 5. Neighbours within the same authored region share parity and polarity (below/above 5). Across a region boundary exactly one of parity and polarity changes.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2. 1 and 2 have different parity within the same box.

# Index

A digit points to its own position in the stated row or column axis. The digit in the pointed cell gives the position of the original cell.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| strips | The marked cells in each straight strip. | No authored strips. |


# Pointing Arrow

Count along the ray by the marked digit to find its target. The mode states whether the target is greater, smaller, equal to the source, or the first 5.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cell | The clue cell. | Required. |
| ray | The cells along the ray, nearest first. | Required. |
| target | The target relationship: greater, less, source or first-five. | Required. |
| source | The cell whose digit the target must match. | Absent; source target requires it. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
let n=D(cell); 1<=n<=|ray| ∧ let t=D(ray[n-1]);
(target="greater" → t>n) ∧ (target="less" → t<n)
∧ (target="source" → present(source) ∧ t=D(unwrap(source)))
∧ (target="first-five" → t=5 ∧ ∀i∈[0,n-1): D(ray[i])!=5)
```

The marked digit names a one-based position within ray. Its target digit is greater, smaller, equal to the source digit, or the first five on the ray, according to target.


Breaks the rule: r1c3=2, r1c1=2, r1c2=1. The selected ray cell equals 2 rather than exceeding it.

# Entropic

Every three consecutive digits contain one from each third of the ordered alphabet. On a two-cell line, the digits come from different thirds.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |
| loop | Whether the line closes, joining its last cell back to its first. | false (open path). |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|𝔄|>0 ∧ |𝔄| mod 3=0
∧ (∀s∈[0,|line|): start(line,3,s,loop) → distinctAt(window(line,3,s,loop),λc:cell: classEntropy(D(c))))
∧ (¬loop ∧ |line|=2 → classEntropy(D(line[0]))!=classEntropy(D(line[1])))
```

Every window of three path positions has one symbol from each equal-sized third of the ordered board alphabet. An open two-cell line uses different thirds. Loop windows wrap. The alphabet size must be divisible by 3.

````markdown
```
````

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=4, r1c3=6. 1, 4, 6 uses the middle third twice and misses the upper third.

# Kropki

A white relation joins values one apart. A black relation joins values where one is twice the other.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| colour | The relationship: white means difference 1; black means ratio 2. | Required. |
| cells | The two marked cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2. | Required. |

## Rule lines

Kropki is a named shorthand for [pair](pair.md):

- `kropki r1c1-r1c2 white` means `pair r1c1-r1c2 difference 1`.
- `kropki r1c1-r1c2 black` means `pair r1c1-r1c2 ratio 2`.

Here `white` and `black` name relationships, not paint instructions. A dot's actual colour stays drawing metadata. For ratio 3, grey or brown dots, difference n, sum n and every other relationship, use [pair's keyword forms](pair.md). Case files state the relationship explicitly. Existing `colour "white"` and `colour "black"` spellings are also accepted.

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|cells|=2 ∧ let a=V(cells[0]); let b=V(cells[1]);
  (colour="white" → |a-b|=1) ∧ (colour="black" → 2*a=b ∨ 2*b=a)
```

A white dot joins values differing by 1; a black dot joins values where one is double the other. The colour parameter names the relationship.

## Example

````markdown
title: Kropki example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
---

```rules

kropki r1c1-r1c2 black
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=4. The black dot joins 2 and 4: 4 is double 2.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=5. The black dot joins 2 and 5: neither is double the other.

# Look And Say

Each listed digit occurs exactly the stated number of times in the cage.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∀p∈counts: countWhere(cells,λc:cell: D(c)=p.digit)=p.count
```

For each {digit,count}, that digit occurs in exactly count cells. Unlisted digits are unconstrained.

# Sandwich

The clue gives the sum of digits strictly between the two crusts, counted from the clue side. State the crust digits and their occurrence policy.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |
| sum | The total the digits or values must add up to. | Required. |
| endpointOccurrences | Whether both endpoints must occur exactly once or at most once. | No extra occurrence condition. |
| crusts | The two crust digits that bound the sandwich. | Lowest and highest board symbols. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|𝔄|>0 ∧ (if present(crusts) then
  ∀i,j∈{t∈[0,|cells|):D(cells[t])∈unwrap(crusts)}: i<j ∧ ¬(∃k∈{t∈[0,|cells|):D(cells[t])∈unwrap(crusts)}:k<j ∧ k!=i) → sum_D(betweenPositions(cells,i,j))=sum
else let lo=𝔄[0]; let hi=𝔄[|𝔄|-1];
  (∀i,j∈[0,|cells|): firstOccurrence(cells,lo,i) ∧ firstOccurrence(cells,hi,j) → sum_D(betweenPositions(cells,i,j))=sum)
  ∧ (endpointOccurrences="exactly-one" → countWhere(cells,λc:cell:D(c)=lo)=1 ∧ countWhere(cells,λc:cell:D(c)=hi)=1)
  ∧ (endpointOccurrences="at-most-one" → countWhere(cells,λc:cell:D(c)=lo)<=1 ∧ countWhere(cells,λc:cell:D(c)=hi)<=1))
```

For custom crusts, sum digits strictly between the first two crust occurrences from the clue. Otherwise use the first lowest/highest symbols and require the between-sum only when both occur. exactly-one requires both once; at-most-one forbids repeated endpoints but allows missing endpoints.

## Example

````markdown
status: read
---

```rules

```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=9. The digit between crusts 1 and 9 totals the clue 2.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=3, r1c3=9. The digit between the crusts totals 3 instead of 2.

# Arrow

A complete one-cell arrow adds effective shaft values to the bulb value. A partial arrow adds face digits to at most the bulb’s face-digit number. A bulb with several cells forms a decimal number in the listed order.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| bulb | The bulb cells, in reading order; several cells form a decimal number. | Required. |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **with aggregates**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
|bulb|>0 ∧ let B = Σ_{i∈[0,|bulb|)} D(bulb[i])*10^(|bulb|-1-i);
  (partial → sum_D(line)<=B)
  ∧ (¬partial → (|bulb|=1 → valueSum(line)=V(bulb[0]))
    ∧ (|bulb|!=1 → sum_D(line)=B))
```

A partial shaft always reads face digits and totals at most the bulb’s decimal face-digit number B. A complete one-cell bulb reads effective shaft and bulb values; a complete multi-cell bulb reads digits and totals B.

# Fog

Part of the grid is covered. Only the lit cells are shown, and entering the right digits lights more of them. Fog is a setup feature of the puzzle, declared in the case-file header, and not a rule line. It defines which cells are visible.

## Case-file header

```yaml
fog:
  initiallyLit: [r2c1, r2c2]      # cells clear at the start; [] for a fully covered grid
  links:                          # absent: neighbourhood reveal. Present, even []: links only
    - trigger: [r1c2]             # every cell here must hold a correct entry
      lights: [r2c3, r2c4, r2c5]  # cells lit when the link fires
```

Cells use `r1c1`, like every cell field in the format. Readers also accept 0-based row-major numbers when the board size is known. `lights` and `initiallyLit` cells are on the grid. `trigger` coordinates may lie off it. `links: []` and a missing `links` mean different things, so the key stays when the list is empty.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| initiallyLit | The cells clear at the start; [] for a fully covered grid. | [] (no cell clear at the start). |
| links | The setter's links, each a trigger set and a set of cells it lights. Absent means neighbourhood reveal; present, even [], means links only. | Absent; neighbourhood reveal. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate, including the entries E, placed, correct and visible. Fog gives visible its definition. A cell is lit when it is visible. L₀ is initiallyLit. A Spot is a coordinate that may lie off the board; a link's trigger is a set of spots, so a trigger off the board is expressible and never correct.

```openrules
type Spot = record{row:position,col:position};
type FogLink = record{trigger:set<Spot>,lights:set<cell>};
play term near(a:cell,b:cell):boolean = |row(a)-row(b)|<=1 ∧ |col(a)-col(b)|<=1;
play term correctAt(p:Spot):boolean = ∃c∈C: row(c)=p.row ∧ col(c)=p.col ∧ correct(c);
play term fires(k:FogLink):boolean = ∀t∈k.trigger: correctAt(t);
```

```text
∀c∈C: visible(c) ↔ (c∈initiallyLit ∨
  (if present(links)
   then ∃k∈unwrap(links): c∈k.lights ∧ fires(k)
   else (given(c) ∧ correct(c)) ∨ ∃a∈C: ¬given(a) ∧ correct(a) ∧ near(a,c)))
```

A cell is visible when it is in L₀, or, with links, when a link that lights it has every trigger cell correct, or, without links, when it is a given typed over with its own digit or lies within one row and one column of a correct non-given entry. The right-hand side does not use visible, so visibility depends on the current entries only and is not a fixed point: lighting a cell fires nothing by itself. A trigger need not be visible, a coordinate off the board is never correct, and erasing an entry hides again what only it showed. An empty trigger is an error, so every link has a trigger.

## Example

````markdown
---
format: open-rules
title: Fog example
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/
status: read
fog:
  initiallyLit: [r1c1, r1c2]
  links:
    - trigger: [r1c2]
      lights: [r2c1, r2c2]
    - trigger: [r2c2, r3c3]
      lights: [r5c5]
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
```
````

The solution has r1c2=3, r2c2=7, r3c3=4. Lit cells for each set of entries:

- No entries: r1c1, r1c2.
- r1c2=3: r1c1, r1c2, r2c1, r2c2. The first link fires.
- r1c2=3, r2c2=7: the same four cells. The second link needs r3c3 too.
- r1c2=3, r2c2=7, r3c3=4: the four cells and r5c5. Both links fire.
- r1c2=3, r2c2=7, r3c3=5: the four cells. 5 is not the digit, so the second link stays off.
- r2c2=7, r3c3=4: r1c1, r1c2 and r5c5. The first link is off again, and the second still fires, because its triggers need entries and not light.

Without `links`, the same header lights a 3×3: with initiallyLit [r5c5] and r1c1=4 entered correctly, r5c5, r1c1, r1c2, r2c1 and r2c2 are lit. A given in r9c9 lights nothing; typing its own digit over it lights r9c9 alone.

# Constructed Regions

Divide the board into connected regions of the stated size. Each region contains different digits. Borders separate regions; joins put cells in the same region.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| size | The number of cells in each constructed region or cage. | Required. |
| borders | Pairs of neighbouring cells that must belong to different regions. | Required. |
| joins | Pairs of cells that must belong to the same region. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∃P:set<set<cell>>: partition(P,C)
  ∧ (∀R∈P: |R|=size ∧ connected(R) ∧ distinct_D(R))
  ∧ (∀p∈joins: |p|=2 ∧ samePartition(P,p[0],p[1]))
  ∧ (∀p∈borders: |p|=2 ∧ ¬samePartition(P,p[0],p[1]))
```

There is a partition of the board into orthogonally connected sets of size cells. Each set has distinct digits; each border separates sets and each join identifies one set. With size equal to the alphabet size, each set contains every symbol.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=1, r1c3=3. The only possible three-cell region repeats 1.

# Cage Shapes

Construct the hidden cages around their clues. Each cage has the stated size, includes its known cells, avoids free cells, and contains different digits adding to its total. Cages are connected and do not overlap.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| size | The number of cells in each constructed region or cage. | Required. |
| hidden | Each hidden cage: its clue cell, total and known member cells. | Required. |
| free | Cells excluded from all hidden cages. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∃chosen:list<set<cell>>:
  |chosen|=|hidden|
  ∧ (∀i∈[0,|hidden|): let h=hidden[i]; let cageSet=chosen[i];
    |cageSet|=size ∧ cageSet⊆C ∧ connected(cageSet) ∧ h.known⊆cageSet
    ∧ cageSet∩free=∅ ∧ h.clue∈cageSet ∧ (∀c∈cageSet: cellIndex(h.clue)<=cellIndex(c))
    ∧ distinct_D(cageSet) ∧ sum_D(cageSet)=h.sum)
  ∧ (∀i,j∈[0,|hidden|): i!=j → chosen[i]∩chosen[j]=∅)
```

There is one size-cell orthogonally connected shape for each hidden cage. It contains known, excludes free, starts at clue in reading order, has distinct digits totalling sum, and overlaps no other hidden cage. With hidden empty, this constraint adds no finished-grid condition.

# Value Modifier

Choose modified cells according to the stated group counts. Their values are their digits times the factor, plus the offset. The same choices apply to every rule that reads values.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| name | The modifier name: doubler or negator. | Required. |
| factor | The multiplier for a modified digit. | Required. |
| offset | The amount added after multiplication. | Required. |
| exactly | The cells in each group and the exact number that must be modified. | Required. |
| count | The number of cells or occurrences to count. | Required. |
| atMostOne | The cells in each group that may contain at most one modified cell. | Required. |
| distinct | Whether modified cells must contain different digits. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **existential**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∃M:set<cell>: M⊆C ∧
(∀G∈exactly: |G∩M|=count) ∧ (∀G∈atMostOne: |G∩M|<=1)
∧ (distinct → distinct_D(M))
∧ (∀c∈C: (c∈M → V(c)=factor*D(c)+offset) ∧ (c∉M → V(c)=D(c)))
∧ (∀meaning∈ValuedRuleMeanings: meaning)
```

There is a shared set M of modified cells. Each exactly group intersects M in count cells; each atMostOne group intersects M in at most one. If distinct, digits in M are distinct. Every valued rule must accept V(c)=D(c)×factor+offset on M and D(c) elsewhere under this same M.

````markdown
```rules
value-modifier name "doubler" factor 2 offset 0 exactly [["r1c1"],["r1c2"]] count 1 atMostOne [] distinct true
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2. Both required modified cells have different digits.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=1. The required modified cells repeat digit 1.

# Zipper

Pairs equally far from the centre have the same sum. On an odd-length line, that sum is the centre digit.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | The cells in order, for example r1c1-r1c2-r1c3. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
(∀i,j∈[0,|line|): i<⌊|line|/2⌋ ∧ j<⌊|line|/2⌋ → D(line[i])+D(line[|line|-1-i])=D(line[j])+D(line[|line|-1-j]))
∧ (|line| mod 2=1 → ∀i∈[0,|line|): i<⌊|line|/2⌋ → |line|>0 ∧ 0<=⌊|line|/2⌋<|line| ∧ D(line[i])+D(line[|line|-1-i])=D(line[⌊|line|/2⌋]))
```

All mirrored pairs cells[i],cells[length−1−i] have the same sum. For odd length, each pair sums to the centre digit.

## Example

````markdown
title: Zipper example
setter: Example

case: ""
library: https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/

zipper r1c1-r1c2-r1c3
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=5, r1c3=3. The end pair adds up to the centre digit 5.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=2, r1c2=5, r1c3=4. The end pair adds up to 6 instead of the centre digit 5.

# Negative

Unmarked neighbouring pairs fail every listed relationship. The scope, direction and exceptions state exactly which pairs are covered.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| relations | The relationships to forbid, each with its operation and any required value. | Required. |
| except | The cell pairs exempt from the negative rule. | Required. |
| within | Groups limiting the pairs covered by the rule. | Absent; no inferred value. |
| direction | The chosen diagonal or neighbour orientation, as named in the definition. | Absent; no inferred value. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
∀a,b∈C: ∀r∈relations:
  cellIndex(a)<cellIndex(b) ∧ orth(a,b)
  ∧ (if present(within) then ∃G∈unwrap(within): a∈G ∧ b∈G else true)
  ∧ (if present(direction) then (unwrap(direction)="horizontal" ∧ row(a)=row(b)) ∨ (unwrap(direction)="vertical" ∧ col(a)=col(b)) else true)
  ∧ ¬(∃p∈except: |p|=2 ∧ {a,b}={p[0],p[1]})
  → ¬pairRelation(r,D(a),D(b))
```

Every orthogonally neighbouring pair in scope and outside except fails every listed relationHolds check over D digits. within limits pairs to a common listed group; direction limits their orientation. Either dot colour exempts the pair from both Kropki negatives when both share except.

The shift relation is defined for integer values.

## Example

````markdown
setter: Example
source: ""
case: ""

status: read
---

```rules
sudoku 9x9
negative relations [{"op":"difference","value":1}] except [] within [["r1c1","r1c2"]]
```
````

Satisfies the rule: r1c2=3, r1c1=1. The unmarked pair does not have forbidden difference 1.

Breaks the rule: r1c2=2, r1c1=1. The unmarked pair has forbidden difference 1.

# Extremum

Each marked digit is smaller than all its unmarked neighbours for a minimum, or larger for a maximum. Exhaustive marking also constrains every unmarked cell.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| type | The mode named in the definition, such as min or max. | Required. |
| cells | The marked cells, for example r1c1-r1c2-r2c2. | Required. |
| exhaustive | Whether every occurrence is marked, so unmarked cells obey the opposite condition. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the notation and every named predicate.

```text
(∀a∈cells: ∀b∈C: orth(a,b) ∧ b∉cells → ((type="min" ∧ D(a)<D(b)) ∨ (type="max" ∧ D(a)>D(b))))
∧ (exhaustive → ∀a∈C: a∉cells → ∃b∈C: orth(a,b) ∧ ((type="min" ∧ D(b)<D(a)) ∨ (type="max" ∧ D(b)>D(a))))
```

Every marked cell is strictly smaller (min) or larger (max) than each orthogonal neighbour outside cells. If exhaustive, every unmarked cell has a strictly smaller (min) or larger (max) orthogonal neighbour.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=1, r2c1=1. An adjacent 1 equals the marked minimum.

# Weighted triple

The third face digit equals the first face digit plus twice the second face digit.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| line | Exactly three cells in order, from the marked start. | Required. |

## Maths

Class: **first-order**.

D(c) is the face digit in cell c. The line is the supplied sequence; its positions start at zero. The [shared predicates](https://rules.sudoku-sleuth.com/predicates.md) define the common notation.

```text
|line| = 3 ∧ D(line[2]) = D(line[0]) + 2 × D(line[1])
```

The third digit is the first digit plus twice the second digit, on a line of exactly three cells.

## Example

```rules
weighted-triple r1c1-r1c2-r1c3
```

Satisfies the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=5. The third digit is 1+2×2=5.

Breaks the rule: r1c1=1, r1c2=2, r1c3=6. The third digit is 6, while 1+2×2=5.
